title: Raise producer_timeout_s to 3000 and record the decision
summary: Change athena.toml [budget] producer_timeout_s from 1800 to 3000, add a decision entry in docs/decisions.md (alternatives: splitting jobs, faster suite, keeping work on timeout; plus reversal), and add a CHANGELOG Unreleased entry. The audience is the Athena operator, who needs producers to stop losing work at the deadline.

defaults_applied.how: The decision entry cites the named job ids and the 5 to 10 minute test build figure as the request's claim, labeled as reported.
The entry is written so an outside reader understands the context, options, and reversal.
Three files only: one config value, one decision entry, one changelog line.
cargo test (including the config parse test) passes and clippy is clean.
The check is that athena.toml parses with 3000 through the repo config test, not that the file was edited.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: The new decision is appended to docs/decisions.md as the next numbered entry after the last existing one (D15 is seen, later ones may exist), in the same heading format.
The three alternatives are recorded as queued follow-ups, not built here.
Reversal means the steps and the signal for setting the value back to 1800 (for example, if no timeouts occur in a stated number of jobs, or cost rises).
The six job count comes from the request; only five job ids are named, so the entry names those five and says the sixth is unnamed.
No code changes; verifier_timeout_s and other budget values are untouched. Other docs that may quote 1800 are checked and updated only if they state the current value.

acceptance_criteria.text: athena.toml [budget] has producer_timeout_s = 3000 and no other budget value changes.

docs/decisions.md has a new entry naming the 1800 to 3000 change, the evidence (the named failed jobs), the alternatives (splitting jobs, a faster suite, keeping work on timeout, each marked queued), and how to reverse it.
CHANGELOG.md has an entry under [Unreleased] describing the producer deadline raise from 1800 to 3000 seconds and why.
Run `cargo test`: the repository config test that parses athena.toml passes with producer_timeout_s = 3000, and the whole suite passes; `cargo clippy` is clean.

out_of_scope: Splitting jobs, speeding up the test suite, or preserving work on timeout (recorded as queued alternatives only)
Changing verifier_timeout_s or other budget settings
departures: Smaller than the reference: a one-value config change plus two prose entries. The verifier's cold cargo test dominates the cost and time.
urgent_reason: Producers keep hitting the 1800 s deadline and losing all their work (six runs), so raising it cuts failed attempts and redo-work retries.
